newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian killers of U.S. woman have sentences cut.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian killers of U.S. woman have sentences cut.

text.p: A Cambodian court has slashed the prison sentences of two men convicted of killing an American tourist and they should be out of jail in less than three years, a court official said on Thursday.

Khmer Rouge defectors Khang Chleu and Sok Khlok were convicted two years ago of robbing and killing Susan Hadden and tour guide Vun Thy as they traveled in a convoy to the ancient Banteay Srei temple in northwest Cambodia on January 15, 1995.
Appellate Court Investigative Judge Ouk Savuth on Wednesday cut their sentences to just five years from terms of between 15 and 18 years, the court official said.
The judge ordered that the new terms would begin from the day of their arrest in late January 1995. Two other suspects in the case escaped from custody in May 1995.
A court official said the sentences were reduced because the men were tried under a law banning the Khmer Rouge, but they had already defected when they were arrested.
"The reason that we reduced the time period of the two men's imprisonment is that they had been Khmer Rouge defectors before the police arrested them," said an official at the appeals court.

The two were sentenced under a 1994 law banning the Maoist Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement, which reneged on a 1991 U.N.-brokered peace pact and has been fighting the coalition government formed after general elections in 1993.
The Khmer Rouge, whose brutal 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, have been torn apart by the defection of thousands of guerrillas since August.

Susan Hadden's husband, James, who was injured in the 1995 ambush, called on King Norodom Sihanouk in September last year to grant a royal amnesty to the two convicted killers of his wife. In a letter to Sihanouk he cited the "moral importance" of forgiving the two men.
The king agreed, but the pardon was apparently shelved after Sihanouk came under fire last October for proposing an amnesty to empty Cambodia's jails of all but the most dangerous criminals.
